I would keep it simple and stay with the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou County best. I am 61, so I would not chase complicated crops that need more labor, more market judgment, or more risk. I would plant winter wheat on all my land, then follow it with summer maize on the same fields after wheat harvest. That is the system I know, it matches the local climate and water conditions, and it gives me two harvests from one year. I would use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable emergence and steady yield, not because I am trying anything fancy. For wheat, I would put more effort into base fertilizer, one irrigation at jointing and one at grain filling if water allows, and a small number of pesticide sprays only when pressure is there. After harvest, I would move quickly into summer maize with no-tillage or very light field preparation, because timing matters more than making the field look perfect. For maize, I would feed nitrogen in stages, keep irrigation limited, and control weeds and insects with a small number of applications. My goal would be steady output, lower labor pressure, and a plan I can carry through myself.
